title: Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol first: from Arminian concessions — if all are made guilty of eternal death by Adam's imputed act alone, God deals more rigidly with men than with demons
pass_a_gloss: I answer first, That we can from the concessions of the Arminians weave a not unlike argument, which yet they themselves will doubtless affirm to be of no moment. For this is to be noted: Although they constantly deny that anyone is damned on account of innate original sin, yet on the contrary their heads are compelled, they acknowledge that the guilt of death even unto all little ones has been derived from the imputation of that actual sin which was committed by Adam. This therefore only being granted, so it is lawful for us to argue: They who establish that God confers all men, infants as well as adults, as guilty of eternal death into strict right, from this alone that there is imputed unto them a sin which is not actual committed in each one's proper person, but perpetrated by Adam, those make God dealing more rigidly with men than with the demons: For no one of the demons is counted guilty except on account of sin committed in his proper person, and from his proper malice; but men, on Arminius's sentence, are constituted guilty of eternal death, only considered as guilty by Divine imputation of Adam's alien sin. Whatever answer they shall have given us, the same we would also retort upon them.
pass_b_english: First I answer: from Arminian concessions we can weave a like argument, which they themselves will doubtless call of no moment. Note this: though they constantly deny anyone is damned for innate original sin, they are forced the other way — they grant that guilt of death has been derived even to all infants from imputation of that actual sin Adam committed. Grant only that, and we may argue: those who hold God puts all men, infants and adults, under strict right as guilty of eternal death merely because a sin not done in each one's own person but by Adam is imputed to them, make God deal more rigidly with men than with demons. No demon is counted guilty except for sin done in his own person from his own malice; yet on Arminius's view men are made guilty of eternal death only as guilty by divine imputation of Adam's alien sin. Whatever reply they give us, we will turn the same back on them.
source_text: Respondeo primo, Posse nos ex concessis Arminianorum non dissimile argumentum texere, quod tamen nullius momenti esse ipsi proculdubio affirmabunt. Nam illud notandum est: Quamvis constanter negent ob innatum peccatum originale damnari quenquam, tamen e contrario coguntur illorum capita, agnoscunt mortis reatum etiam in parvulos omnes esse derivatum ex imputatione actualis ejus peccati quod ab Adamo admissum fuit. Hoc itaque solummodo concesso sic licet nobis argumentari: Qui statuunt Deum omnes homines, tam infantes quam adultos, aeternae mortis reos in strictum jus conferre, ex eo solum quod imputatur illis peccatum quod non actuale in propria uniuscujusque persona commissum, sed ab Adamo perpetratum, illi faciunt Deum rigidius agentem cum hominibus quam cum diabolis: Nam nemo diabolorum reus censetur nisi ob peccatum in propria persona, et ex propria malitia commissum; at homines, ex sententia Arminii, rei mortis aeternae constituuntur, tantum considerati uti alieni peccati Adami ex imputatione Divina rei. Quicquid responsi nobis dederint, idem nos et illis regeremus.
